title: Diffusion bonding of AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high entropy alloy to TiAl alloy

nodes.label: Lightweight TiAl must be joined reliably to a dissimilar structural alloy (EHEA) for high-temperature components
Bonding temperature controls interdiffusion, reaction-layer sequence/thickness and interface morphology, hence joint shear strength has an optimum
As-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic HEA and commercial TiAl alloy as base metals
XRD: EHEA reflections indexed to FCC + B2; TiAl reflections to TiAl + Ti3Al
BSE: EHEA lamellar eutectic (white FCC, grey B2); TiAl lath-shaped Ti3Al with dark-grey TiAl
Base metals: EHEA = lamellar FCC + B2 eutectic; TiAl = dual-phase TiAl + Ti3Al
Diffusion bonding at 0.6-0.8 Tm of the lower-melting base (EHEA, 1361 C); HEA sluggish diffusion favours the upper end
Bonding temperature 900 / 950 / 1000 C at 0.5 h, 15 MPa, after 800 C / 30 MPa preheat
Vacuum diffusion bonding of polished EHEA and TiAl blocks
No bonding defects at any temperature; EHEA-side layer flat, TiAl-side rugged; convex structure where B2 meets TiAl

attrs.image_note: No pores or cracks at 30 um scale in a-c; 'Convex' arrows in (a) point to bulges of the diffusion zone at B2

nodes.label: Sound metallurgical bond at all temperatures, with convex bulges and penetration in the diffusion zone near B2
Acicular precipitates in FCC coarsen with T; precipitates in B2 grow strongly at 950 C and almost vanish at 1000 C

attrs.image_note: (b) right shows large white blocky/acicular precipitates in B2; (c) B2 region nearly clean

nodes.label: Fe/Cr-rich sigma phase precipitates from B2 near 600 C and disappears at 1000 C in AlxCoCrFeNi
Acicular B2 in FCC coarsens with temperature; sigma precipitates in B2 grow up to 950 C then dissolve at 1000 C
EPMA maps: Zone A four layers; Co enriched in layer II, Al/Ni-rich rods in layer I, Ti/Al rise toward TiAl; Zone B three layers

attrs.image_note: Co map shows a red band in layer II; Al/Ni rods mirror the BEI rods of layer I; Nb confined to TiAl side

TEM-EDS: Co and Ni segregate in layer II; punctate phase in layer II rich in Cr, Fe, Nb

nodes.label: Layer compositions: layer II Co/Ni-rich with Al, Ti; layer III Ti-rich blocky + Ni-bearing lamellar phase; punctate FCC-like Cr/Fe particles
XRD of EHEA-side fracture surface: AlNi2Ti/AlCo2Ti, FCC, B2 and tau3-Al3NiTi2 reflections

Growth activation energies: A-I 125.2, A-II 165, A-III 304.7, A-IV 314.8; B-II 398, B-III 184.4, B-IV 358.3 kJ/mol

nodes.label: Rodlike B2 layer grows first (lowest Q); tau3 grows preferentially near B2 (Q 184 vs 305 kJ/mol near FCC)
Preferential tau3 growth near Ni-rich B2 (and unequal/Kirkendall diffusion) produces convex structure and penetration

attrs.basis: argued; Kirkendall named in packet summary

nodes.label: Average shear strength 168, 449, 170 MPa at 900, 950, 1000 C

attrs.image_note: Bar chart; 950 C error bar ~+/-80 MPa, 900 C bar has almost none

nodes.label: Joint shear strength peaks at 449 MPa for 950 C bonding
A critical IMC thickness exists beyond which joint properties deteriorate
Interlocking from convex/penetration raises strength; IMC overgrowth beyond critical thickness and loss of convexity at 1000 C lowers it
Cracks run along the interface; secondary cracks enter layer I/B2; crack into B2 arrested by blocky FCC (950 C)

attrs.image_note: Main crack between EHEA and TiAl visible at 1000x; the specific II/III location is not resolvable at this magnification

nodes.label: TiAl-side fracture surface at 950 C is macroscopically flat with cleavage-like facets
Brittle fracture initiating at the Al(Co,Ni)2Ti / tau3+TiAl (II/III) interface
Coarsened acicular B2 lowers FCC ductility, letting secondary cracks propagate through layer I
950 C gives the strongest EHEA/TiAl joint; FCC and B2 sides develop different reaction-layer sequences
Choose bonding temperature giving enough diffusion for interlocking but IMC thickness below the critical value

notes: Packet has no introduction; HYP nodes inferred. Lost: Table 2 point compositions A-F, per-layer detail of Zone B, F2/F3 (specimen/process schematics, not opened). The argument branches into (i) layer identification (chemistry maps + line scans + XRD + SAED converging on m24), (ii) growth kinetics (m25->m28->m30->m31->m32) and (iii) strength/fracture (m33-m40). Multimodal core: phase-per-layer claims need chemistry and crystal structure read from maps/line scans/SAED to be registered onto layers seen in BSE/TEM images (proposed mm_op correlate_colocated_modalities). Image audit: F12 'parabolic growth' is a curve through 3 temperatures at fixed time, not a time law; Q values from 3-point ln w fits with one clear outlier (A-III); F9 cannot separate AlNi2Ti from AlCo2Ti; F14a-c do not resolve that cracks sit at the II/III interface; F8 near-B2 Al trough is text-silent. m27 counteracts m34 applies to the 1000 C regime only (overthick IMC); at 900 C the loss is insufficient interlocking via m11. Joint shear strength typed PRP/value fit poor: it is a property of an assembly, see comments.
